chunks: That is indicated by what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Safwan from 'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a young boy who marries a young girl, they inherit from each other. He said: 'If their parents are the ones who married them, then yes.' I asked: 'Is the father's divorce valid?' He said: 'No.'

The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And if a man contracts marriage for his son while he is a minor and specifies a dowry, then the father dies, the dowry is from the principal of his estate before division, unless the boy has wealth at the time of the contract, in which case the dowry is from his wealth, not the father's.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage and inheritance for young children in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the validity of *nikah al-sighr* (marriage of minors) arranged by parents, while clarifying that the father’s right to divorce is not absolute in this context. The juristic discussion highlights the distinction between the father’s estate and the child’s independent wealth for the payment of the dowry (*mahr*), reflecting the Shia principle that financial obligations follow the ownership of the assets at the time of the contract. This ruling underscores the protective legal status of minors within the family structure, ensuring their financial rights are preserved regardless of the father’s death.
